adjudication_records.issue_text: Legacy writes in goroutines capture the request context which is canceled when the handler returns, causing legacy writes to fail with context-canceled errors and silently diverge from unified storage (needs a detached context like context.WithoutCancel)

adjudication.rationale: In Mode3 Create/Delete/Update/DeleteCollection, the legacy write is executed in a goroutine after the function returns, but the goroutine derives its context from the incoming `ctx` (e.g., `context.WithTimeoutCause(ctx, ...)`). If the caller/request cancels `ctx` when the handler returns, the derived context will also be canceled immediately, causing the legacy write to fail with `context canceled` (or the timeout cause never being reached) and silently diverging from unified storage since the goroutine ignores the error except for metrics (no log/propagation). This behavior is directly visible in the new async legacy write blocks.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Data race on the shared object in Create/Update: the object returned in the response is concurrently mutated by the legacy goroutine (setting resourceVersion, UID, timestamps), corrupting the response; objInfo's UpdatedObject may also be invoked concurrently

adjudication.rationale: In `DualWriterMode3.Create`, after `d.Storage.Create(...)` returns `created`, the code immediately returns that object while also launching a goroutine that calls `d.Legacy.Create(ctx, obj, ...)` using the same `obj` pointer passed into the request. If `Storage.Create` returns (or reuses) the same underlying object as `obj` (a common pattern in Kubernetes-style storage), then the legacy goroutine can mutate the same object instance concurrently with the caller/API server encoding the returned `created`, causing a data race/corrupted response. Similarly, `Update` launches an async `d.Legacy.Update(..., objInfo, ...)` after calling `d.Storage.Update` with the same `objInfo`; even though the storage call completes before the goroutine starts, the async legacy call can operate on shared object state referenced by `objInfo` after the handler has returned.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Mode 3 Update passes raw objInfo to legacy instead of the snapshotted updated object via updateWrapper, so legacy recomputes the update against the legacy copy and can persist different content or fail validation

adjudication.rationale: In `DualWriterMode3.Update`, the previous logic that snapshotted the updated object and wrapped `objInfo` (via `updateWrapper{updated: ...}`) before writing to Legacy has been removed. The new code calls `d.Storage.Update(...)` and then asynchronously calls `d.Legacy.Update(..., objInfo, ...)` passing the original `objInfo` unchanged. Since `rest.UpdatedObjectInfo` is typically evaluated against the storage being updated, Legacy can recompute a different updated object based on its own current state, leading to divergence or validation differences, matching the finding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Storage failures in Create/Update are recorded with the legacy metrics function (recordLegacyDuration), misattributing unified store outages as legacy failures

adjudication.rationale: In `pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go`, the error paths for unified storage operations call the legacy metrics recorder with the storage timer. In `Create`, when `d.Storage.Create(...)` returns an error, it invokes `d.recordLegacyDuration(true, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startStorage)` instead of a storage recorder. Similarly in `Update`, when `d.Storage.Update(...)` fails, it calls `d.recordLegacyDuration(true, ...)` using `startStorage`. This would misattribute unified store failures as legacy failures in metrics.

adjudication_records.issue_text: DeleteCollection records legacy duration via recordStorageDuration, corrupting storage metric series with legacy timings
Legacy NotFound errors (and context-canceled errors) are now counted as failures instead of being tolerated, making the legacy write errors metric persistently noisy

adjudication.rationale: In dualwriter_mode3.go the previous Delete implementation explicitly tolerated NotFound (apierrors.IsNotFound) for both unified and legacy deletes and only treated other errors as failures. This diff removes the apierrors import and all NotFound checks, and the legacy operations are now done asynchronously with a 10s timeout via context.WithTimeoutCause; any resulting NotFound or context timeout/cancellation will be passed into d.recordLegacyDuration(err != nil, ...) as a failure. That changes the legacy write error metrics semantics and can make them persistently noisy compared to the prior behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Delete builds an enriched logger 'log' with name/kind but injects bare d.Log into the context, losing correlation fields in nested storage logs
matched_golden_ids: The context is being created with d.Log instead of the log variable that was initialized with additional context values (name, kind, method). This means those values won't be propagated to the logging context.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate points out that an enriched logger variable is created but the context is populated with the un-enriched d.Log, causing added fields (name/kind/method) to be lost—same underlying issue as the golden comment.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Delete success path records metric with 'name' as label while error path uses options.Kind, splitting the metric into incompatible label sets

Unbounded fire-and-forget goroutines spawned per Create/Update/Delete/DeleteCollection write with no concurrency limit, worker pool, or backpressure, creating unbounded concurrent load on the legacy backend

adjudication.rationale: In `pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go`, the new Mode3 implementation spawns a new `go func(){...}` on every successful `Create`, `Update`, `Delete`, and `DeleteCollection` to perform the legacy write asynchronously (each wrapped only with a 10s `context.WithTimeoutCause`). There is no concurrency limiter (semaphore/worker pool), queue, or backpressure mechanism shown in the diff, so under high request rates this can create an unbounded number of concurrent goroutines and corresponding concurrent calls to the legacy backend.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Async goroutines hold references to request object graphs, delaying GC of potentially large objects

adjudication.rationale: In `pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go`, several methods now launch async legacy writes via `go func() { ... }()` (e.g., `Create`, `Delete`, `Update`, `DeleteCollection`). These goroutines close over request-scoped values like `ctx`, `obj` (a `runtime.Object`), `objInfo`, validation funcs, and `options`/`listOptions`. Because the goroutine can run up to the 10s timeout (`context.WithTimeoutCause(..., time.Second*10, ...)`), it will retain references to these potentially large object graphs until it completes, delaying GC. This is a real, diff-grounded performance/memory concern, not a functional correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Goroutines capture the request-scoped ctx which is cancelled when the HTTP handler returns, potentially aborting legacy writes immediately; should use context.WithoutCancel/background context

adjudication.rationale: In `dualwriter_mode3.go`, Mode3 now performs legacy writes asynchronously in goroutines that derive their context from the request-scoped `ctx` (e.g., `go func() { ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeoutCause(ctx, 10s, ...) ... d.Legacy.Create/Delete/Update/DeleteCollection(...) }()`). If the original `ctx` is the HTTP request context, it is typically canceled when the handler returns; since these goroutines run after returning, the parent cancellation can immediately cancel the derived context and abort the legacy write, defeating the intended dual-write behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Async legacy writes have no retry/ack/queue, so any failure (timeout, cancellation, transient DB error) permanently diverges the two stores with silent data loss

adjudication.rationale: In `pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go`, legacy writes for `Create`, `Delete`, `Update`, and `DeleteCollection` were changed from synchronous calls to fire-and-forget goroutines (`go func(){ ... d.Legacy.*(...) ... }()`). Errors from these legacy operations are not returned to the caller and (unlike the prior synchronous version) are not logged at all—only metrics are recorded. Additionally, the goroutine uses `context.WithTimeoutCause(ctx, ...)` with the request `ctx` as parent, so if the request context is canceled when the handler returns, the legacy write can be canceled/never complete. There is no retry/queue/ack mechanism in the diff, so transient failures/timeouts can permanently leave LegacyStorage diverged from Storage without any surfaced failure, matching the finding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Update legacy write passes raw objInfo rather than the persisted/updated object, so legacy may compute a different result and diverge from storage

adjudication.rationale: In `pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go`, `Update` now calls `d.Storage.Update(...)` and then asynchronously calls `d.Legacy.Update(...)` passing the original `objInfo` unchanged (`d.Legacy.Update(ctx, name, objInfo, ...)`). The prior implementation explicitly computed the updated object and wrapped `objInfo` in an `updateWrapper` so legacy would use the same persisted/returned object from storage (`updated: obj`). With the wrapper removed, legacy may re-run `UpdatedObject` and can produce a different object (e.g., differing defaults/resourceVersion), causing divergence between unified storage and legacy writes—matching the finding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Delete's recordStorageDuration uses object name as a metric label instead of options.Kind, causing unbounded Prometheus label cardinality

adjudication.rationale: In `DualWriterMode3.Delete`, after a successful storage delete it calls `d.recordStorageDuration(false, mode3Str, name, method, startStorage)`. The third argument is `name` (the object name) whereas other methods consistently pass `options.Kind` as that label value (e.g., Create/Get/List/DeleteCollection). Using object names as a Prometheus label value can create unbounded label cardinality, and the diff clearly shows this incorrect argument being passed.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Update (~line 135) records storage failure via recordLegacyDuration instead of recordStorageDuration, polluting legacy metrics

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go, the Mode3 Update method measures the storage update duration (startStorage := time.Now()) and on storage error incorrectly calls d.recordLegacyDuration(true, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startStorage) instead of d.recordStorageDuration(...). This misattributes unified-store failures/timing to legacy metrics, matching the finding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: DeleteCollection goroutine (~line 180) records legacy duration with recordStorageDuration, polluting storage metrics
matched_golden_ids: In DualWriterMode3's DeleteCollection method, when a storage operation fails, recordStorageDuration is incorrectly called with recordLegacyDuration instead.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both point to the same bug in DualWriterMode3.DeleteCollection: the code records the legacy duration using the storage-duration recorder (i.e., the wrong metric function is called in the failure path), leading to polluted/mislabeled storage metrics.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Legacy writes in dualwriter_mode3.go are fire-and-forget with no error logging, retry, or backpressure, causing silent permanent divergence between unified and legacy stores

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go the legacy-side writes (Create/Delete/Update/DeleteCollection) were changed from synchronous calls with error logging to fire-and-forget goroutines that discard errors and do not log them. E.g., Create runs Legacy.Create in a goroutine with a timeout and only calls d.recordLegacyDuration(err != nil, ...) without any log or returning an error; same for Delete and Update. This makes legacy write failures effectively silent to operators/callers and can leave Storage and Legacy permanently divergent with no visibility beyond metrics. (Also, DeleteCollection’s goroutine mistakenly calls d.recordStorageDuration instead of recordLegacyDuration, further reducing correct observability.)

adjudication_records.issue_text: Goroutines in dualwriter_mode3.go derive from the request context, so legacy writes are cancelled when the HTTP request completes; should use context.WithoutCancel or a background context with only the timeout

adjudication.rationale: In `dualwriter_mode3.go`, the legacy writes are executed asynchronously in goroutines (e.g., `Create`, `Delete`, `Update`, `DeleteCollection`) using `context.WithTimeoutCause(ctx, 10s, ...)` where `ctx` is the incoming request context. Since these goroutines run after the main method returns, the parent request context is likely to be canceled when the HTTP request finishes, which would immediately cancel the derived timeout context and can prevent the legacy operation from running/completing. This can break the intended dual-write behavior (legacy write may be skipped). Using `context.WithoutCancel(ctx)` or `context.Background()` (then applying timeout) would avoid this.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Mode 3 tests won't compile: TestMode3_Create, List, Delete, DeleteCollection, and Update call NewDualWriter(Mode3, ls, us, p) but only TestMode3_Get declares p (prometheus.NewRegistry())

adjudication.rationale: The finding claims Mode 3 tests won't compile because `p` is only declared in `TestMode3_Get`. However, the diff also removes a local `p := prometheus.NewRegistry()` from `dualwriter_mode1_test.go` while still calling `NewDualWriter(..., p)`, which strongly indicates there is already a package-level `p` in scope (defined elsewhere in the package tests) that these tests are intended to use. In that case, the Mode 3 tests that call `NewDualWriter(Mode3, ls, us, p)` will compile, and `TestMode3_Get` is merely shadowing the package-level `p` with a local one.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Update legacy write no longer uses the updateWrapper, so legacy's UpdatedObject is computed against possibly stale legacy state, allowing divergence or optimistic-concurrency conflicts that are silently dropped

adjudication.rationale: In `DualWriterMode3.Update`, the previous implementation computed the updated object once and used an `updateWrapper` so both Storage and Legacy saw the same updated object (and Legacy was given the post-US object via `updated: obj`). The new code calls `d.Storage.Update(...)` directly, then asynchronously calls `d.Legacy.Update(...)` with the original `objInfo` (no wrapper). That allows Legacy’s update path to re-run `UpdatedObject` against Legacy’s own current object (which can differ from Storage), potentially producing different writes or optimistic-concurrency conflicts; and because the legacy update is done in a goroutine with no error propagation/logging, these conflicts can be silently ignored.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Wrong metrics recorded on error paths: Create storage-failure path calls recordLegacyDuration for a storage failure, and DeleteCollection legacy goroutine calls recordStorageDuration for a legacy operation

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows incorrect metrics functions being called on specific paths in `pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go`: (1) In `Create`, when `d.Storage.Create(...)` returns an error, it calls `d.recordLegacyDuration(true, ..., startStorage)` even though the timed operation was the storage create (should be `recordStorageDuration`). (2) In `DeleteCollection`, the legacy-delete goroutine times `d.Legacy.DeleteCollection(...)` but then calls `d.recordStorageDuration(err != nil, ..., startLegacy)` instead of `recordLegacyDuration`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Inconsistent label cardinality in Delete (~L95): success path records name as the "kind" argument while every other call site passes options.Kind, exploding metric label cardinality
matched_golden_ids: Inconsistency: using name instead of options.Kind for metrics recording differs from other methods.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate flags that the Delete method records metrics using `name` as the "kind" label/argument, whereas other call sites use `options.Kind`, which is exactly the inconsistency described in the golden comment.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Legacy Delete errors are no longer filtered for NotFound, so benign NotFound errors during migration count as failures in metrics, generating false divergence alarms

adjudication.rationale: In `DualWriterMode3.Delete`, the previous implementation explicitly ignored NotFound errors via `apierrors.IsNotFound(errLS)` for both unified store and legacy store deletes. This diff removes the `k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/api/errors` import and the NotFound checks entirely, and the legacy delete is now done asynchronously with `d.recordLegacyDuration(err != nil, ...)`, so a NotFound from `d.Legacy.Delete(...)` will be recorded as an error. That matches the finding: benign NotFound deletes can now be counted as failures in metrics/alerts.

adjudication_records.issue_text: New unit tests in dualwriter_mode3_test.go never assert that legacy Create/Delete/Update/DeleteCollection was invoked (no AssertExpectations, goroutine races with teardown), so they verify mocks rather than the new async dual-write behavior

adjudication.rationale: In the new `pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3_test.go` tests, legacy-side calls are not actually verified. The tests set up `mock.Mock` expectations via `m.On(...)` (e.g., `TestMode3_Create`/`TestMode3_Update`), but never call `m.AssertExpectations(t)` / `AssertCalled`, so the tests will pass even if `d.Legacy.*` is never invoked. This is especially relevant because the implementation now performs legacy writes asynchronously in goroutines (e.g., `Create`, `Delete`, `Update`, `DeleteCollection` in `dualwriter_mode3.go`), meaning the test can complete before the goroutine runs, further reducing the tests’ ability to validate the new async dual-write behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No test covers the legacy write timeout path (10s context timeout), e.g. blocking legacy storage where the write is abandoned

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds new asynchronous legacy-write behavior with a hard 10s timeout via `context.WithTimeoutCause(..., time.Second*10, errors.New("legacy ... timeout"))` in Mode3 `Create`, `Delete`, `Update`, and `DeleteCollection` (each starts a `go func()` that calls the legacy store). The newly added tests in `pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3_test.go` only validate the main Storage path and immediate return values; they do not simulate a blocking legacy storage call nor assert behavior/metrics when the legacy goroutine hits the 10s timeout and abandons the write. So the finding (missing test coverage for the timeout path) is specific and grounded in the diff, but it is a test-gap rather than a proven functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No test verifies the sync/async error split: that a storage error suppresses the legacy write and a legacy error does not propagate to the caller

adjudication.rationale: In `dualwriter_mode3.go`, the mode-3 write path is explicitly split: storage write happens synchronously and returns errors to caller, while legacy write is launched asynchronously in a `go func()` with a timeout and its error is only recorded via metrics (e.g., `Create`, `Delete`, `Update`, `DeleteCollection`). If storage fails, the legacy goroutine is not started (e.g., `Create`: early return before the `go func()`). The added tests in `pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3_test.go` assert only the caller-visible return values (success vs error) but do not verify (a) that legacy is *not invoked* when storage returns an error, nor (b) that a legacy error does *not propagate* to the caller (and since legacy is async, the tests also don’t wait/assert on legacy invocation). Thus the finding about missing test coverage for the sync/async error split is grounded in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: TestMode3_Create error case has dead/misleading mock setup: setupLegacyFn configures a Legacy.Create expectation that is never called and never asserted

adjudication.rationale: In `TestMode3_Create`, the error-case test configures `setupLegacyFn` to expect `LegacyStorage.Create(...)` on `failingObj`, but `DualWriterMode3.Create` (as modified) returns immediately when `d.Storage.Create` fails and never calls legacy (the legacy write is only started in a goroutine after a successful storage create). The test also does not call `m.AssertExpectations(t)`, so the unused legacy expectation is neither validated nor will it fail, making the mock setup dead/misleading as claimed.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Update error path records storage failures via recordLegacyDuration instead of recordStorageDuration, misattributing storage errors to legacy metrics

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go, Update() measures storage update duration (startStorage := time.Now(); res, async, err := d.Storage.Update(...)). On the error path it calls d.recordLegacyDuration(true, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startStorage) before returning. This records a Unified Store (storage) failure into the legacy metrics, misattributing the error as the finding states (it should likely call recordStorageDuration).

adjudication_records.issue_text: DeleteCollection legacy goroutine calls recordStorageDuration for the legacy call, recording legacy durations as storage durations

adjudication.rationale:
In `DualWriterMode3.DeleteCollection`, the legacy write is executed in a goroutine, but its duration is recorded via `d.recordStorageDuration(...)` instead of a legacy-specific recorder. The diff shows:

```go
_, err := d.Legacy.DeleteCollection(...)
d.recordStorageDuration(err != nil, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startLegacy)
```

This misclassifies legacy call timings as storage timings, leading to incorrect metrics/observability behavior introduced by the change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Delete success path passes 'name' as the kind label to recordStorageDuration while the error path passes options.Kind, producing inconsistent metric labels

adjudication.rationale: In `DualWriterMode3.Delete`, the error path records storage duration with `options.Kind` (`d.recordStorageDuration(true, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startStorage)`), but the success path uses `name` as the third argument (`d.recordStorageDuration(false, mode3Str, name, method, startStorage)`). This will produce inconsistent metric label values (kind vs resource name) for the same operation.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Mode 3 Update now passes raw objInfo to the async legacy update instead of the object computed from storage, so legacy can compute a different object than unified storage — with no test coverage

adjudication.rationale: In `DualWriterMode3.Update`, the previous implementation computed an updated object once and ensured legacy got the same object via `updateWrapper` (first `objInfo.UpdatedObject(...)`, then legacy `Update` with `updated: obj`). The new code calls `d.Storage.Update(..., objInfo, ...)` and then asynchronously calls `d.Legacy.Update(..., objInfo, ...)` (raw `objInfo`), so legacy may recompute a different updated object than the one persisted in unified storage. The added `TestMode3_Update` only checks return values from the unified store and does not assert that legacy receives the same computed object, so this divergence is untested.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Update no longer pre-Gets the object; missing tests for update-creates-object (forceAllowCreate=true) and NotFound propagation

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `DualWriterMode3.Update` no longer does a pre-`Get` (`old, err := d.Storage.Get(...)` block was removed) and now calls `d.Storage.Update(...)` directly. In `dualwriter_mode3_test.go`, `TestMode3_Update` only covers a successful update and a generic storage error; it does not cover the create-on-update path (`forceAllowCreate=true`) nor a NotFound-style error propagation case. This is a specific, diff-grounded test gap for the changed Update behavior rather than a proven functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Mode 3 Delete now returns immediately on any storage error, so NotFound from unified aborts the legacy delete, breaking deletion of legacy-only objects — with no test coverage

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go, Delete now does `res, async, err := d.Storage.Delete(...)` and immediately returns on any `err` (lines: `if err != nil { ... return res, async, err }`). The previous implementation explicitly tolerated `apierrors.IsNotFound(err)` from Storage and still attempted the legacy delete, enabling deletion of legacy-only objects. The new code removed the `apierrors.IsNotFound` handling (and even removed the apierrors import), so a NotFound from unified storage will abort the legacy delete path. The updated tests in dualwriter_mode3_test.go only cover unified delete success and generic error; they do not cover the Storage-NotFound/legacy-delete-still-happens scenario.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Integration tests (playlist_test.go mode 3 subtests) don't verify legacy store contents; without synchronization/polling, async legacy writes are unverified and dropping them entirely would pass tests

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes DualWriter mode 3 to perform legacy writes asynchronously in goroutines with timeouts (e.g., Create/Delete/Update/DeleteCollection now `go func(){ ... d.Legacy.<op>(...) }()` in `dualwriter_mode3.go`). The newly added integration subtests in `playlist_test.go` for mode 3 only call `doPlaylistTests(...)` with `DualWriterDesiredModes` set to `Mode3`, but the diff shows no additional assertions or synchronization/polling to ensure the async legacy writes completed or that legacy storage contains the expected data. Given mode 3 reads are from unified storage, these mode 3 integration tests could pass even if legacy writes are dropped or never happen, making this a concrete test-coverage gap introduced by the async change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: TestMode3_List case name is stale: it references 'not implemented' behavior but List is now implemented in mode 3

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows Mode3.List is now implemented (calls d.Storage.List and records metrics) and the TestMode3_List table still includes a case name saying "not implemented". That’s a stale/misleading test description, but it doesn’t indicate a functional defect or substantive review issue—just wording.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Legacy writes in Create/Delete/Update/DeleteCollection are fire-and-forget goroutines with no error surfacing, retry, or reconciliation, causing silent data divergence between stores

adjudication.rationale: In `pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go`, legacy writes are now performed in unjoined goroutines: `Create` (legacy `Create` in `go func(){...}`), `Delete` (legacy `Delete` in `go func(){...}`), `Update` (legacy `Update` in `go func(){...}`), and `DeleteCollection` (legacy `DeleteCollection` in `go func(){...}`). None of these goroutines return errors to the caller or log failures; they only record a duration/error flag via metrics. This makes legacy-write failures effectively non-blocking and can allow the caller to observe success while the legacy store write fails, creating potential for unnoticed divergence. The diff does not implement any retry/reconciliation mechanism.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Legacy-write goroutines capture request-scoped context, so they are cancelled when the parent request ends; need detached context without parent cancellation

adjudication.rationale: In DualWriterMode3 the legacy writes are executed asynchronously in goroutines (e.g., Create/Delete/Update/DeleteCollection) that derive their context from the request-scoped ctx: `go func() { ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeoutCause(ctx, 10s, ...) ... d.Legacy.Create(ctx, ...) }()`. Because this new context is a child of the incoming request context, it will be canceled when the parent request completes (common in HTTP/gRPC request contexts), so the best-effort legacy write can be prematurely canceled, causing missed/partial legacy writes and divergence. The diff does not detach from parent cancellation (e.g., via context.WithoutCancel or Background + copied values), matching the finding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: DeleteCollection legacy goroutine calls recordStorageDuration instead of a legacy duration metric, corrupting both metrics

adjudication.rationale: In `pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go` within `DeleteCollection`, the legacy write is executed in a goroutine (`d.Legacy.DeleteCollection(...)`), but the duration is recorded with `d.recordStorageDuration(err != nil, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startLegacy)` instead of a legacy metric (e.g., `recordLegacyDuration`). This misattributes legacy timings/errors to the storage metric and omits the legacy metric, corrupting both measurements.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Update storage error path calls recordLegacyDuration(true, ...) for a Storage.Update failure — wrong store and wrong metric

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go, DualWriterMode3.Update() measures startStorage then calls d.Storage.Update(...). On the error path it records `d.recordLegacyDuration(true, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startStorage)`, which is the legacy metric function even though the failure occurred in unified/storage and the duration being measured is for the storage call. This is mismatched store/metric on the Storage.Update failure path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Delete success path passes object name instead of options.Kind as the kind label, exploding metric label cardinality

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go Delete(), the success path calls `d.recordStorageDuration(false, mode3Str, name, method, startStorage)`, passing `name` where other paths pass `options.Kind` (e.g., the error path uses `options.Kind`). If that parameter is used as the "kind" label, this will create per-object label values and explode metric cardinality.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Mode3 tests assert on mocks without waiting for legacy goroutines, causing data races and flaky teardown panics

adjudication.rationale: The diff does make Mode3 fire legacy writes/deletes/updates in background goroutines, and the new tests generally do not wait for those goroutines to finish. However, the finding claims the tests “assert on mocks” and that this causes “data races and flaky teardown panics.” In the shown tests, there are no mock call-count/assertion checks (e.g., no AssertExpectations/Counts), and the mocks are not tied to *testing.T in a way shown here that would make late calls panic at teardown. From the diff alone, the claimed data races/teardown panics are not verifiable.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Delete uses d.Log in klog.NewContext instead of the enriched log variable, discarding built logger values

adjudication.rationale: In `DualWriterMode3.Delete`, an enriched logger is built (`log := d.Log.WithValues("name", name, "kind", options.Kind, "method", method)`), but the context is set with the base logger instead (`ctx = klog.NewContext(ctx, d.Log)`), so the values on `log` are not propagated via the context to downstream calls like `d.Storage.Delete(...)` / `d.Legacy.Delete(...)`. This is a concrete, diff-grounded observability issue, but it doesn’t clearly break functional behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Duplicated write-both boilerplate across Mode3 methods leads to drift and wrong-metric/wrong-label bugs; should be extracted into a helper

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows duplicated Mode3 boilerplate with clear drift that already causes wrong metrics/labels in multiple methods, not just a maintainability concern. Examples: (1) Create(): on Storage.Create error it calls d.recordLegacyDuration(...) instead of recordStorageDuration. (2) Update(): on Storage.Update error it calls d.recordLegacyDuration(...) instead of recordStorageDuration. (3) Delete(): success path records storage duration with the object name as the “kind” label (d.recordStorageDuration(false, mode3Str, name, ...)), and it also sets the context with d.Log (dropping the enriched log values). (4) DeleteCollection(): legacy async path calls d.recordStorageDuration(...) instead of recordLegacyDuration. These are verifiable wrong-metric/wrong-label behaviors introduced by the duplicated logic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Hardcoded 10s timeout magic number with fabricated error string repeated 5x; should be a named/configurable constant

adjudication.rationale: In `pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go`, multiple async legacy operations wrap the context with `context.WithTimeoutCause(ctx, time.Second*10, errors.New("... timeout"))` (e.g., in `Create`, `Delete`, `Update`, `DeleteCollection`). The 10s duration is hardcoded and repeated, and the timeout-cause strings are hand-written in each site, making it a maintainability/configurability concern rather than a correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: updateWrapper may now be dead code in the package after Mode3's Update no longer uses it

adjudication.rationale: In `pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go`, the previous `Update` implementation explicitly wrapped `objInfo` with `&updateWrapper{...}` before calling `Storage.Update` and `Legacy.Update`. That whole `updateWrapper` usage has been removed in the new `Update` implementation (it now calls `d.Storage.Update(...)` directly and then calls `d.Legacy.Update(...)` in a goroutine with the original `objInfo`). From this diff alone we can verify `Mode3` no longer uses `updateWrapper`, so it’s reasonable to flag that `updateWrapper` might now be dead/unused code and worth checking/cleaning up, though the diff doesn’t show whether other modes/files still reference it.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Create storage-error branch records legacy duration despite no legacy operation occurring

adjudication.rationale: In `pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go` `Create`, the error path after `d.Storage.Create(...)` fails calls `d.recordLegacyDuration(true, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startStorage)` even though no legacy operation was attempted and the timer started for the storage call (`startStorage := time.Now()`). This misattributes storage failures/duration to legacy metrics, which is a concrete, diff-verifiable correctness issue in the new metrics logic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Async fire-and-forget legacy writes with no retry, queue, or reconciliation cause silent permanent divergence between stores when legacy writes fail

adjudication.rationale: In DualWriterMode3, legacy writes for Create/Delete/Update/DeleteCollection were changed from synchronous calls (previously logged on error) to fire-and-forget goroutines with a 10s timeout (e.g., Create: `go func() { ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeoutCause(ctx, ...); _, err := d.Legacy.Create(...); d.recordLegacyDuration(...) }()`). These goroutines do not return errors, do not retry/queue, and (critically) derive their context from the request `ctx`, which is commonly canceled once the main operation returns—so legacy writes can be canceled immediately and fail silently (no `log.Error` in the goroutine), causing permanent divergence between Storage and Legacy.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Legacy write goroutines inherit the request context which is canceled when the handler returns, causing legacy writes to be silently dropped with context canceled errors; should use context.WithoutCancel or background context

adjudication.rationale: In DualWriterMode3, legacy writes were changed to run asynchronously in goroutines (Create/Delete/Update/DeleteCollection) using a context derived from the incoming `ctx`: e.g. `go func() { ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeoutCause(ctx, 10s, ...) ... d.Legacy.Create(ctx, ...) }()`. Because the goroutine inherits the request context, if that context is canceled when the handler/request finishes, the derived context will be canceled immediately and the legacy write can be skipped/fail with `context canceled` (only metrics are recorded; no retry/propagation). This behavior is introduced by the diff and can cause dropped legacy writes/inconsistency; using `context.WithoutCancel(ctx)` or `context.Background()` + logging values would avoid coupling to request cancellation.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Update passes raw objInfo to legacy Update instead of wrapping the exact updated object, so legacy result can diverge from storage result

adjudication.rationale: In `DualWriterMode3.Update`, the new code writes to `d.Storage.Update(...)` and then asynchronously calls `d.Legacy.Update(ctx, name, objInfo, ...)` using the original `objInfo` (see the goroutine call). The previous implementation explicitly computed the updated object and wrapped it (`updateWrapper{updated: ...}`) so the legacy update used the exact same updated object that storage produced. With the new approach, legacy will recompute the updated object against legacy's own current state, which can diverge from storage’s result if the two stores aren’t identical—matching the finding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: objInfo's UpdatedObject callback may not be safe for concurrent invocation; running it in a background goroutine after the request completes races on captured state

adjudication.rationale: In DualWriterMode3.Update, the diff changes behavior to call d.Storage.Update(...) synchronously, then invokes d.Legacy.Update(...) in a background goroutine using the same objInfo instance (go func() { ... d.Legacy.Update(ctx, name, objInfo, ...) }()). If Legacy.Update internally calls objInfo.UpdatedObject, that callback may be executed after the main request returns and possibly a second time (once during Storage.Update, once during Legacy.Update). The diff doesn’t prove a concurrent invocation, but it does introduce asynchronous/later invocation and potential double-use of objInfo, which can be unsafe if objInfo captures request-scoped mutable state or is not intended to be reused after the request completes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Data race on the created object: the object returned to the caller is passed to Legacy.Create in a goroutine with no synchronization

adjudication.rationale: In `DualWriterMode3.Create`, the function returns to the caller while launching a goroutine that calls `d.Legacy.Create(ctx, obj, ...)` using the same `obj` pointer passed into `Create` (and often the same object instance that `Storage.Create` may have mutated/returned). This unsynchronized sharing of a mutable `runtime.Object` across goroutine boundaries can lead to a data race if the caller (or other code) reads/mutates the object after `Create` returns while the legacy write is still executing.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Tests never verify legacy writes happen; AssertExpectations is never called on legacy path mocks, so a regression dropping legacy writes passes green

adjudication.rationale: In the new Mode3 tests (pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3_test.go), legacy-path expectations are set on a testify mock (e.g., TestMode3_Create sets m.On("Create", ...) for LegacyStorage, TestMode3_Update sets m.On("Update", ...) for LegacyStorage), but the tests never call m.AssertExpectations(t) / AssertCalled on those legacy interactions. Since DualWriterMode3 now performs legacy writes asynchronously in goroutines (Create/Delete/Update/DeleteCollection), a regression that drops or never executes the legacy call could still let these tests pass green because unmet expectations aren’t asserted anywhere in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Wrong metric on Create error path: recordLegacyDuration called when Storage fails, should be recordStorageDuration

adjudication.rationale: In `pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go` `Create()`, the code measures `startStorage := time.Now()` before calling `d.Storage.Create(...)`. On error, it calls `d.recordLegacyDuration(true, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startStorage)` even though the failed operation is the Storage create; this should be `recordStorageDuration(...)` to attribute the duration/error to Storage, not Legacy.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Wrong metric on Update error path: recordLegacyDuration(true, ...) recorded on storage failure

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go Update(), on Storage.Update failure the code calls d.recordLegacyDuration(true, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startStorage) even though the failure occurred in the unified Storage path (the legacy write happens later in a goroutine). This misattributes storage failures to legacy metrics (and also uses startStorage), so the finding is directly verified by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: DeleteCollection legacy goroutine calls recordStorageDuration for the legacy write instead of recordLegacyDuration

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go within DeleteCollection(), the legacy write is performed in a goroutine and timed with startLegacy := time.Now(), but the code records the result using d.recordStorageDuration(err != nil, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startLegacy) instead of recordLegacyDuration. This misattributes legacy-operation latency/error metrics to storage metrics, which is a concrete defect visible in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Delete success path uses name as the kind label, causing label cardinality blowup with object names as label values

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go, Delete() records storage duration on the success path with `d.recordStorageDuration(false, mode3Str, name, method, startStorage)`—passing `name` where other calls consistently pass `options.Kind` (e.g., error path uses `options.Kind`). If that argument is used as the "kind" label, this will populate it with per-object names, causing high-cardinality metrics and incorrect labeling.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Delete discards the constructed enriched logger, storing unadorned d.Log into the context so legacy goroutine log lines lose name/kind/method fields

adjudication.rationale: In DualWriterMode3.Delete, an enriched logger is built (`log := d.Log.WithValues("name", name, "kind", options.Kind, "method", method)`), but the context is set with the unadorned logger (`ctx = klog.NewContext(ctx, d.Log)`) instead of `log`. The subsequent legacy delete runs in a goroutine using that `ctx`, so any `klog.FromContext(ctx)` logging inside legacy storage would miss the name/kind/method fields. This is a concrete diff-grounded observability/instrumentation issue, not a functional correctness bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Mock-based tests are timing-dependent: fire-and-forget goroutines have no wait/synchronization so tests may finish before the legacy write runs

adjudication.rationale: In `pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go`, legacy writes are now done in fire-and-forget goroutines (e.g., `Create`, `Delete`, `Update`, `DeleteCollection` all `go func() { ... d.Legacy.<op>(...) }()` with no synchronization). The new mock-based tests in `pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3_test.go` return immediately after the Unified Store call and do not wait for or assert that the legacy goroutine ran, so they can finish before the legacy write executes. This makes the tests not actually validate the newly introduced async legacy behavior and could become timing-sensitive if expectations/assertions are added later.
